images.seen: Near East at end of -5100 with --compare-cliopatria (Cliopatria has nothing before 3400 BCE, so its panel is empty): ubaid-period holds the alluvium, Gulf coast, Jazira, Assyria and Amuq with the Samarra disc cut out; halaf-culture is gone (dissolved this year). Matches the dossier. A one-cell-wide sliver of Ubaid runs between the Samarra disc and Babylonia along the Tigris, and one small hole sits near the Euphrates at about 38.3E 36.8N. Both are boundary artefacts, not worth a patch.

World at end of -5001 with --compare-cliopatria (empty panel, as above): 29 archaeological cultures, each in its own region and none far from it; no speckle, no holes of note, no jumps. Green Sahara cultures is a very large block, but it is the dossier's deliberate 'Sahara less Egypt, less the Capsian country, less the Gobero disc' and the packet flags nothing there.

issues.what: ubaid-period keyframe snap at -5100: the ledger gain from halaf-culture (473 cells) does not cover all of the keyframe, so the state snaps by 395 cells that Halaf never held (Dayr Az Zawr 65, Sanliurfa 53, Ninawa 46, +15 more). Both use the same region spec (Jazira + Assyria + Aleppo 90 km, less Samarra); the keyframe is just wider than the Halaf circles.

patch_check: no patch written; nothing to check
problems: The Ubaid page says 'In Northern Mesopotamia the period runs only from about 5300 to 4300 BC' and 'In Northern Syria and southeastern Turkey, the Ubaid follows upon the Halaf period'; the phase table gives Ubaid 3 as 5100-4900 (Pournelle 2003) or 5200-4600 (Harris 2021). That supports the Ubaid holding the north from -5100. The page names the Amuq, Mersin, Norsuntepe and Arslantepe but not Dayr Az Zawr, Sanliurfa or Nineveh, so the extra 395 cells rest on the region name 'Northern Mesopotamia' alone, not on a dated sentence. I left them, since a patch event would only restate the snap. The packet's own tables show no size-rule conflicts, skipped events, unresolved regions, hierarchy relations or colour clashes in this window.
